acqinfo.head: Acquisition Information
acqinfo.p: These records came to the Library of Virginia in a 2026 transfer of records from Bedford County Public Schools under accession number 54916.

custodhist.head: Custodial History
custodhist.p: These records initially came to the Library of Virginia in a 2026 donation from the Bedford County Historical Society (BCHS)to the Private Papers collection. Because the BCHS did not have legal authority to transfer public records, Bedford County Public Schools was contacted and opted to transfer the records under their authority. Normally, these non-permanent records would not be maintained, but due to the absence of pre-1936 student cumulative files (Long-term documentation) in the Bedford County Public Schools records, they have been retained.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: These records were organized chronologically by school name by Bedford County Historical Society volunteers.

bioghist.head: Historical Information
bioghist.p: Context for Record Type: On February 21, 1818, the Virginia legislature passed a school bill which appropriated $45,000 annually from the Literary Fund for the education of poor children. (The Literary Fund was established in 1810 with passage of a bill to appropriate "certain escheats, confiscated, and forfeited lands" for the "encouragement of learning.") Under the provisions of the 1818 School Act, each county court was required to appoint five to fifteen commissioners to establish and/or administer schools for children of the poor.

Prior to 1818, county courts were given the option of whether to appoint a Board of School Commissioners. In 1869 a uniform system of free schools was made compulsory, and the new system was administered by a county superintendent and by school trustees whose general duties were administration of school matters and construction and maintenance of school buildings. The Virginia public school system was racially segregated until the mid-twentieth century.

Locality History: Bedford County was named probably for John Russell, fourth duke of Bedford, who served as secretary of state for the southern department from 1748 to 1751 and had general supervision of colonial affairs. It was formed from Lunenburg County in 1753, and parts of Albemarle and Lunenburg Counties were added in 1755. The county court first met on 5 May 1754. The county seat is the town of Bedford.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Content
scopecontent.p: Bedford County (Va.) School Records, 1914-1953 ca., is mainly comprised of teacher grade and attendance books for individual schools. The books contain student names, grade levels, grades and attendance notes, teacher remarks, and some cumulative statistics for the year, 1914-1935 ca. Box 27 contains materials from the Bedford County Education Association, 1944-1953.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p:
This collection is arranged into the following series:
Series I: School Records, 1914-1953 ca., are loosely arranged chronologically.
